brand.name: Pativ
brand.tagline: Orders go from the guest's phone straight to the kitchen

landing.metaTitle: Pativ: QR menu and ordering for cafés
landing.metaDescription: Guests scan the QR on the table, pick dishes, and the order appears on the kitchen screen and the waiter's phone.
landing.title: Orders go from the guest's phone straight to the kitchen
landing.lead: Runs on the phones you already have, no new devices. We build the menu in three languages from a photo of your paper one.
landing.trial: The first month is free. No card needed.
landing.heroAlt: The demo café's menu on a guest's phone

menu.title: QR menu
menu.text: A menu with photos in three languages. Guests order from their own phone.
menu.alt: A dish open on the guest's phone: a large photo, the price and an Add button with the total
menu.p1: Each dish opens with a large photo, its description and calories.
menu.p2: Guests pick the quantity, leave a note for the kitchen and see the total before adding.
menu.p3: Guests can call the waiter or ask for the bill from their phone.

waiter.title: Waiter app
waiter.text: New orders, calls and bill requests, table by table.
waiter.alt: The waiter app's floor: nine tables, each coloured by what it needs
waiter.p1: A table's colour says what it needs: a new order, food to serve or the bill.
waiter.p2: Under the number: how long the table has waited and its total so far.
waiter.p3: Calls and bill requests ring, so nobody waves for long.

kitchen.title: Kitchen screen
kitchen.text: Tickets arrive in order and turn red after 12 minutes.
kitchen.alt: The kitchen screen with tickets by stage
kitchen.note: Each café picks its kitchen screen's language: Armenian, Russian or English.
kitchen.p1: One tap moves a ticket on: New, Cooking, Ready.
kitchen.p2: The table that has waited longest is always shown at the top.
kitchen.p3: The cook can mark a dish as sold out, and guests can no longer order it.

admin.title: Owner admin
admin.text: Menu, tables, staff and the day's reports.
admin.alt: The owner admin's menu on a phone: breakfast dishes with photos, prices and a Sold out today button
admin.p1: Every dish with its photo and price, section by section.
admin.p2: One tap on Sold out today hides a dish from guests, and the list clears in the morning.
admin.p3: Tables with their QR codes, staff logins and the day's sales are here too.

step1.title: Sign up
step1.text: Create an account and add your café. No card needed.

step2.title: Add your menu
step2.text: Take photos of your paper menu. We read the dishes and prices and translate them, and you check everything before it goes live.

step3.title: Print the QR codes
step3.text: Put them on the tables, and connect the kitchen and waiter devices with a six-digit code.

offline.text: If the connection drops, the guest's order waits on their phone and goes out by itself when it's back.

export.text: Download the menu, orders and bills as CSV files for Excel or Google Sheets.

telegram.text: When a table waits too long, you and your team get a message.

merge.name: Kissing Dishes
merge.howTo: Swipe to slide the dishes: two of a kind kiss and turn into a bigger dish. Grow a bunch of greens into a whole festive table.

slice.name: Salad Panic
slice.howTo: Swipe to slice the panicking veggies before they fall. Don't break grandma's teapot. The golden pomegranate scores ×10.

runner.name: Waiter Run
runner.howTo: Tap to jump, tap again in the air to jump higher. Swipe down to slide under awnings and signs. Collect the coffee cups.

fighter.name: Kitchen Clash
fighter.howTo: The arrows walk, jump and raise a pot lid (down). The round buttons swing the spoon, swing the pan and throw a tomato; on a keyboard, Z, X and C. Win two rounds to become head chef.

platformer.name: Café Cat
platformer.howTo: The arrows walk, the big button or Space jumps. Grab the fish and sausages, stomp the mice, dodge the hot burners and the chef's broom, and steal his plate of fish.

weak.page: Text is hard to read on this colour with this theme. Guests keep the theme's page colour.
weak.line: Text on tags would be hard to read on this colour. Guests see it in the thin lines; tags get a shade closer to your page.

brand.wordmarkHint: Your name as a picture. It replaces the typed name at the top of the menu. A PNG with a transparent background works best. You can upload two versions: dark lettering for light backgrounds and light lettering for dark ones. With only one picture, it's used everywhere.

pos.title: POS connection
pos.intro: If the café already runs a POS, Pativ sends every accepted order into it. Waiters don't type orders twice, and the POS prints the kitchen ticket, the bill and the fiscal receipt as it does today.
pos.notInV1: Changes after sending (cancelled dishes, "can't make") are not sent to the POS: change them there too. Pativ sends no payments or fiscal data.

vendorHints.test: Sends nothing out. Orders show up below under "Recent sends". Good for trying it out.
vendorHints.webhook: Mersoft, Norksys, 1C-based systems or any other POS. Each order is POSTed as JSON to your address, signed with a key.
vendorHints.iiko: iiko Cloud API (api-ru.iiko.services). Create the API key in iikoWeb.
vendorHints.syrve: iiko's international edition (api-eu.syrve.live). Create the API key in Syrve App.
vendorHints.poster: Find the personal API token in Poster's settings. Orders arrive as online orders.

pos.phoneHint: If Poster refuses orders without a phone, enter the café's number.
pos.secretHint: The key is kept in a secure vault and never shown again. To change it, enter a new one.
pos.menuHint: Load the POS menu. Dishes with matching names are matched automatically; pick the rest from the list.
pos.notMatched: {count, plural, one {# dish not matched} other {# dishes not matched}}
pos.notMatchedHint: Orders with these dishes won't reach the POS, and the waiter will see why.
pos.activeOn: Accepted orders go to the POS
pos.activeOff: Off: orders don't go to the POS
pos.testQueued: The test order is queued. The result shows below.
